GUIDED TUTORIAL

Create a Liquidity Reference Ledger

Map potential buy-side/sell-side objectives and distinguish a reference level from an entry trigger.

TUTORIAL MATERIALS
  • A completed NQ, ES, GC or CL session chart
  • A fixed definition of trading day/week and session timezone
  • A spreadsheet or journal

Track prerequisites: entry-models-execution, futures-contract-roll-risk

01

WORKFLOW

Follow the practice sequence

  1. Step 1

    Before reviewing the outcome, record the product, expiry, data feed, timezone and session definition.

  2. Step 2

    Mark the last completed day and week highs/lows, plus the chosen session high/low.

  3. Step 3

    Mark equal-high/equal-low clusters using a tolerance fixed in ticks or points before reviewing the move.

  4. Step 4

    Label potential BSL above highs and SSL below lows. Describe these as chart-based hypotheses, not visible orders or measured resting liquidity.

  5. Step 5

    Choose one possible opposing pool as an objective and record what separate trigger would be required before a trade could be considered.

02

DELIVERABLE

What to create

A dated liquidity ledger with at least six premarked pools, tolerance/session rules and a separate trigger column.

CONCEPT LIBRARY

Relevant lessons

Liquidity →Buy-Side Liquidity (BSL) →Sell-Side Liquidity (SSL) →Equal Highs (EQH) →Equal Lows (EQL) →Prior Day High / Low (PDH / PDL) →Prior Week High / Low (PWH / PWL) →Session High / Low →Opposing Liquidity / Draw on Liquidity →
Use this tutorial for historical chart study and rule writing. Do not infer an edge or trade from a practice example. Futures are leveraged and can cause substantial losses.
